newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's PM sets jobs, housing as priorities.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's PM sets jobs, housing as priorities.

text.p: Algeria's Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, echoing President Liamine Zeroual guidelines to fight unemployment and housing shortages, said on Wednesday that creating jobs was among his government's top priorities.

"Every Algerian, and morever every politician, longs for a better response to the problems of scarce housing, job-creation and purchasing power," said Ouyahia as he emerged from the first meeting of his three-party coalition cabinet.
Ouyahia was also quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS as saying the government would step up economic reforms.
Over than two million people, mostly under the age of 30, are jobless out of a workforce of about six million. The oil and gas producing country lacks around two million housing units.
On Monday, Zeroual urged the cabinet to speed up economic reforms and launch a huge programme to provide employment.

The government, formed last week from the three main parties in the newly elected National Assembly (lower house), has began drawing up a programme. This will have to be presented later in July to the house for a confidence vote.
Ouyahia, dropping poll campaigning attacks on his now junior partners in the government, said he was pleased to be leading a coalition government.
"It is in the tradition that alliances, often bearing different shades of views, are forged. But the synthesis is built around the main problems facing the country," he said.

Seven ministers from the Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Solution (MPS) are in the government alongside the same number of ministers and junior cabinet members from the former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN).
The National Democratic Rally (RND), grouping Zeroual's supporters, controls the key posts. The RND, MPS and FLN have respectively 156, 69 and 62 seats in the 380-member lower house.
